sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Four-year bachelor's/equivalent and minimum GPA3.0; UChicago degree fits. International status accepted;
individual mathematical preparation assessed. [s1]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Columbus MATH-PHD, mandatory Theoretical Math subplan for these interests. Use passport spelling;
prepare web-generated course PDF. Submit early because referee invitations follow submission by a few days.
[s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
grad-info@math.osu.edu; research page invites contacting faculty directly about research. Current capacity
unknown. [s1] [s7]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Apply, then activate OSU name.# and use Admissions Uploader for additional documents/referee edits. [s1]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Cohort page explicitly Autumn 2027 and October 1, 2026 opening; standby year and IELTS threshold
inconsistent across sources. [s1] [s2] [s4]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Conflict]
Regular deadline December 1, linked to Autumn 2027 context (December 1, 2026 inferred). Standby January
28 is undated in instructions but explicitly stale January 28, 2026 on current cohort page; 2027 standby date
unconfirmed. Timezone not stated. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
December 1 regular application for maximum department/university funding; Autumn 2027 year inferred from
cohort header. Fee-waiver request due November 30, 2026 before application submission. [s1] [s2]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
Actual separate reference deadline not stated; invitations arrive days after submission. Submit early and target
complete file by regular December 1 deadline; confirm permissible letter grace. [s1]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Official English reports, if needed, by application deadline. GRE if chosen must arrive from ETS; no separate
GRE receipt date verified. [s1] [s4]

Supporting documents [Unresolved]
Regular application December 1; additional documents and updated transcripts accepted through Admissions
Uploader, but no final supplementary cutoff specified. [s1]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Waitlist maintained until April 15, but this is not itself an explicit offer acceptance deadline. Use offer. [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Central minimum old TOEFL79/new4.0, IELTS6.5, DET120; Math instructions still state IELTS7.0 and PhD page
recommends TOEFL95/IELTS7 plus speaking20/6.5. US-degree exemption is clearer. TA spoken certification
remains separate. [s1] [s4] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
US bachelor's received by matriculation exempts admission English testing. Most international students still
face writing assessment and non-native GTAs oral certification before duties. [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; omission will not harm PhD application. If submitted, official ETS delivery. [s1] [s6]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional under PhD GRE policy; do not confuse MAQRM instructions (nonconsideration) with PhD. [s1]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Color legible scan of official transcript, front/back, every attended university including transfer institutions;
advising reports/web printouts unacceptable. Updated grades can be uploaded. [s1]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Required PDF produced by department web tool, then uploaded as Other/Portfolio/Research experience.
Strongly preferred over manually prepared list; tables/spreadsheet exports discouraged. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
For each course: school, term, grade, level, content, books/authors, covered chapters/topics. Keep each course
together on a page. [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three; names, emails, institutional addresses and phone/country codes. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
Not established in the public sources checked; verify this item in the program portal or with graduate
admissions.
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
A few days after application submission, each referee receives upload link. [s1]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Yes; activates after submission. Applicant then gets OSU username and can add/edit/delete requests via
Admissions Uploader. [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Follow up on receipt; public instructions explain uploader access but exact letter-completion display not
established. [s1]

Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Referee requests can be edited/added/deleted after posting; already-submitted letter replacement and
cross-cycle reuse unverified. Recommender may email grad-info@math.osu.edu only if online upload
impossible. [s1]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required PDF, preferably no more than3 pages. Prompt paraphrase: organized evidence of mathematical
ability, promise and trajectory. [s1]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required PDF, preferably no more than3 pages. Prompt paraphrase: mathematical
development/ability/promise; relevant challenges may be explained. Font/spacing not specified. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Relevant personal/academic barriers can be addressed in SOP/CV; separate essay not specified. [s1]
Research-interest statement; Research proposal; Publications list; Scholarship essays; Other short
answers / materials [Unresolved]
No distinct prompt/requirement identified beyond SOP/CV/course list and optional documents;
length/format/upload-link rules for separate item unverified. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Optional relevant PDF documents, maximum 10 pages. Do not submit whole thesis/book; department says it
will not read those. [s1]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required; theoretical order: analysis, algebra, other pure math, applied math, other; reverse chronological
within each. Include detailed content/texts/grades and keep each course together. [s5]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Numeric incoming 2027 stipend unverified. Nine-month GTA plus tuition and100% health-insurance-premium
subsidy. Bus/activity/union/recreation fees may remain. Do not treat summer as guaranteed. [s3]
Years of support [Standing rule]
GTA renewable on academic progress; exact multi-year guarantee unverified. Summer historically available to
>90% of requesters. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
All admitted PhDs offered academic-year GTA; university fellowships explicitly include international applicants.
[s2] [s3]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Approximately20 hours/week including teaching/preparation/grading. Mandatory compensated four-week
pre-autumn Headstart training. Progress required for renewal. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Admission includes GTA offer; fellowship nomination selection. No separate incoming support form found. [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University/Distinguished University fellowships (first12 months and possible later years); continuing
Presidential/department fellowships, SGA/Rhodus, research assistantships and travel funds. [s3]

Application fee [Standing rule]
USD70 international (USD60 domestic), nonrefundable. [s2]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
Department financial-need form opens October 1; request before application and by November 30, 2026.
Public wording includes PhD applicants, no nationality exclusion stated. [s2]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Number theory
Stefan Patrikis
Galois representations, motives, Shimura varieties and automorphy. [s7] [s8]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2025 · Compatibility of canonical l-adic local systems on Shimura varieties
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Jennifer Park
Arithmetic geometry, points/counting and algebraic curves. [s9] [s12]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 institutional record · On Rational Points on Classifying Stacks and Malle's Conjecture
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
David Anderson
Algebraic geometry and algebraic combinatorics; Schubert calculus, flag varieties, degeneracy loci, equivariant
cohomology and K-theory. [s11] [qbr11_q1] [qbr11_q2] [qbr11_q3] [qbr11_q4]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2025 · Čech cohomology of infinite projective spaces, flag manifolds, and related spaces
With Matthias Franz; revised 17 December 2025; author bibliography says to appear Canadian Mathematical Bulletin.
Cohomology rings of infinite flag manifolds and products.
Research evidence: 2025 · Infinite flags and Schubert polynomials
Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 13, e36; published 10 February 2025. Infinite-dimensional flag geometry, degeneracy loci and
equivariant positivity.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier interests: Schubert/toric geometry, group actions and combinatorial positivity; recent-paper audit pending.

Maria Angelica Cueto
Combinatorial algebraic geometry, tropical and nonarchimedean geometry; tropical lifts of tritangents, real
algebraic curves, surface singularities and moduli. [s11] [qbr12_q5] [qbr12_q6] [qbr12_q7] [qbr12_q8] [qbr12_q9]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · A lifting partition theorem for tropical tritangent classes to smooth space sextic curves
With Hannah Markwig and Yue Ren; submitted 19 May 2026. Lifting multiplicities in tropical tritangent classes. Verified on official
author bibliography and indexed primary arXiv; direct arXiv open failed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Tropical methods for building real space sextics with totally real tritangent planes
With Yoav Len, Hannah Markwig and Yue Ren; submitted 30 December 2025, revised 29 May 2026. Tropical methods construct
real sextics with prescribed real tritangents and discuss arithmetic consequences.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier interests: Tropical/non-Archimedean geometry, valuations and singularity topology; recent-paper audit pending.
Representation theory
Sachin Gautam
Representation theory and quantum groups; Yangians, quantum loop algebras, braid groups, flat connections,
difference equations and integrable systems; links to equivariant K-theory of quiver varieties. [s10] [s11]
[qbr13_q10] [qbr13_q11] [qbr13_q12] [qbr13_q13]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · On the uniqueness of Yangians
With Curtis Wendlandt and Siwei Xu; preprint 27 June 2025; official bibliography updated 4 November 2026 lists to appear
Algebras and Representation Theory (2026). Uniqueness of homogeneous quantization of polynomial current algebras.
Research evidence: 2026 · An abelian formula for the quantum Weyl group action of the coroot lattice
With Valerio Toledano Laredo; revised 22 May 2026; author bibliography gives IMRN(2026). Formula for quantum Weyl-group
action, with application to equivariant K-theory of Nakajima quiver varieties.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier interests: Yangians, quantum loop/elliptic groups, difference equations; recent-paper metadata pending.

prepare web-generated course PDF. Submit early because referee invitations follow submission by a few days.

face writing assessment and non-native GTAs oral certification before duties. [s4]

Optional; omission will not harm PhD application. If submitted, official ETS delivery. [s1] [s6]

Color legible scan of official transcript, front/back, every attended university including transfer institutions;
advising reports/web printouts unacceptable. Updated grades can be uploaded. [s1]

Required PDF produced by department web tool, then uploaded as Other/Portfolio/Research experience.
Strongly preferred over manually prepared list; tables/spreadsheet exports discouraged. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
For each course: school, term, grade, level, content, books/authors, covered chapters/topics. Keep each course
together on a page. [s5]

Number and type [Standing rule]
Three; names, emails, institutional addresses and phone/country codes. [s1]

Not established in the public sources checked; verify this item in the program portal or with graduate
admissions.
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
A few days after application submission, each referee receives upload link. [s1]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Yes; activates after submission. Applicant then gets OSU username and can add/edit/delete requests via
Admissions Uploader. [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Follow up on receipt; public instructions explain uploader access but exact letter-completion display not
established. [s1]

Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Referee requests can be edited/added/deleted after posting; already-submitted letter replacement and
cross-cycle reuse unverified. Recommender may email grad-info@math.osu.edu only if online upload
impossible. [s1]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required PDF, preferably no more than3 pages. Prompt paraphrase: organized evidence of mathematical
ability, promise and trajectory. [s1]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required PDF, preferably no more than3 pages. Prompt paraphrase: mathematical
development/ability/promise; relevant challenges may be explained. Font/spacing not specified. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Relevant personal/academic barriers can be addressed in SOP/CV; separate essay not specified. [s1]
Research-interest statement; Research proposal; Publications list; Scholarship essays; Other short
answers / materials [Unresolved]
No distinct prompt/requirement identified beyond SOP/CV/course list and optional documents;
length/format/upload-link rules for separate item unverified. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Optional relevant PDF documents, maximum 10 pages. Do not submit whole thesis/book; department says it
will not read those. [s1]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required; theoretical order: analysis, algebra, other pure math, applied math, other; reverse chronological
within each. Include detailed content/texts/grades and keep each course together. [s5]

Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Numeric incoming 2027 stipend unverified. Nine-month GTA plus tuition and100% health-insurance-premium
subsidy. Bus/activity/union/recreation fees may remain. Do not treat summer as guaranteed. [s3]
Years of support [Standing rule]
GTA renewable on academic progress; exact multi-year guarantee unverified. Summer historically available to
>90% of requesters. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
All admitted PhDs offered academic-year GTA; university fellowships explicitly include international applicants.
[s2] [s3]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Approximately20 hours/week including teaching/preparation/grading. Mandatory compensated four-week
pre-autumn Headstart training. Progress required for renewal. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Admission includes GTA offer; fellowship nomination selection. No separate incoming support form found. [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University/Distinguished University fellowships (first12 months and possible later years); continuing
Presidential/department fellowships, SGA/Rhodus, research assistantships and travel funds. [s3]

USD70 international (USD60 domestic), nonrefundable. [s2]

Department financial-need form opens October 1; request before application and by November 30, 2026.
